newsitem.title: OMAN: ANZ unit to sell Oman branches to new bank.
newsitem.headline: ANZ unit to sell Oman branches to new bank.

text.p: ANZ Grindlays Bank, part of the Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd, said on Sunday it would sell its two branches in Oman to a new Omani bank.
But ANZ will maintain a minority shareholding in The Oman Savings and Finance Bank SAOG, it said in a statement.
It said ANZ will provide technical and management support, including the secondment of three senior officers to the new bank for two years.
ANZ declined to give the price it was selling the branches for, but a Muscat stock broker said the bank would receive around 3.5 million rials for its assets and goodwill.
A Central Bank of Oman statement said the new bank would start operating in the next few months. It will have a paid-up capital of 20 million rials.
ANZ will put up five percent of the capital.

Four companies and four government pension funds will be the new bank's major shareholders, putting up the bulk of 60 percent of the capital. The remaining 40 percent will be offered to the public through the Muscat Securities Market.
The four firms are Oman National Holding Co, Oman National Insurance Co, National Life Insurance and Galfar Engineering and Contracting Co.
